polynomial.title: What is a Polynomial?
polynomial.intro: A polynomial is an algebraic expression made up of terms that contain variables raised to whole number powers, added or subtracted together.

notes.title: Tips and Tricks

poly.content: The word 'polynomial' comes from 'poly' (many) + 'nomial' (terms). So a polynomial has many terms!

distribute.content: IMPORTANT: When subtracting, distribute the negative sign to ALL terms in the second polynomial! This is the most common mistake.

notes.tip1: Always write polynomials in standard form (highest degree first) to avoid confusion.
notes.tip2: Like terms have the EXACT same variables with the EXACT same exponents. 2x² and 3x² are like terms, but 2x² and 2x are NOT.
notes.tip3: When multiplying, remember: multiply coefficients AND add exponents. x² · x³ = x⁵

standard.title: Standard Form
standard.description: Write terms in order from highest to lowest degree:

adding.title: Adding Polynomials
adding.description: To add polynomials, combine like terms (terms with the same variable and exponent).

subtracting.title: Subtracting Polynomials
subtracting.description: To subtract polynomials, distribute the negative sign, then combine like terms.

multiplying.title: Multiplying Polynomials
multiplying.description: To multiply a monomial by a polynomial, use the distributive property: multiply the monomial by EACH term.

factoring.title: Factoring Out the GCF
factoring.description: Factoring is the reverse of multiplying. We find the Greatest Common Factor (GCF) of all terms and factor it out.

anatomy.title: Anatomy of a Polynomial
anatomy.caption: Understanding each part of a polynomial

factoring.title: Factoring with GCF
factoring.caption: Find what's common and pull it out!
factoring.step1Detail: GCF of 6 and 9 is 3, GCF of x² and x is x. So GCF = 3x

degree.title: Degree of a Polynomial:
degree.content: The degree is the highest exponent in the polynomial. It tells us important information about the polynomial's behavior!

multiply.title: Exponent Rule for Multiplication:
multiply.content: When multiplying powers with the same base, ADD the exponents: xᵃ · xᵇ = x⁽ᵃ⁺ᵇ⁾

multiplying.title: Example 3: Multiplying by a Monomial
multiplying.step1: Distribute 4x to each term inside the parentheses

exercise1.question: What is the degree of the polynomial 5x³ - 2x² + 7x - 1?
exercise1.explanation: The degree is the highest exponent, which is 3 in the term 5x³.

exercise2.question: Add: (3x² + 5x - 1) + (2x² + 2x + 8). What is the constant term in the result? Enter the number.
exercise2.explanation: Result is 5x² + 7x + 7. The constant term is 7.

exercise3.question: Which of the following is a binomial?
exercise3.explanation: A binomial has exactly TWO terms. 2x + 5 has two terms, so it's a binomial.

exercise4.question: Subtract: (3x² - 5x + 2) - (x² + 3x - 6). What is the constant term in the result? Enter the number.
exercise4.hint: Distribute the negative, then combine. Pay attention to the constant terms: 2 - (-6)
exercise4.explanation: Distribute negative: 3x² - 5x + 2 - x² - 3x + 6. Combine: 2x² - 8x + 8. Constant is 8.

exercise6.question: Factor: 6x² + 9x. If we write it as 3x(ax + b), what is the value of a? Enter the number.
exercise6.hint: Find the GCF first. GCF of 6 and 9 is 3, and both terms have at least x.
exercise6.explanation: GCF is 3x. Factor it out: 3x(2x + 3). So a = 2.

area.title: 📐 Area Calculations
area.description: If a rectangle has length (x + 3) and width (x + 2), its area is the polynomial x² + 5x + 6.

physics.title: 🚀 Physics & Motion
physics.description: The height of a thrown ball over time is often modeled by polynomials like h = -16t² + 32t + 48.

conclusion.title: Mastering Polynomials!
conclusion.summary: Polynomials are the foundation of algebra! You've learned how to identify, classify, add, subtract, multiply, and factor them.
conclusion.takeaway1: Polynomials are sums of terms with whole number exponents
conclusion.takeaway2: Combine like terms when adding or subtracting
conclusion.takeaway3: Distribute carefully when subtracting (watch those signs!)
conclusion.takeaway4: Factoring is the reverse of multiplying
